title: Karl Data Narrative: Undocumented immigrants in Texas had lower criminal convicti
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: Undocumented immigrants in Texas had lower criminal conviction rates than native-born Americans]
[Source: Cato Institute (2020)]

Even the libertarian right's data says it: immigrants commit crimes at lower rates. The 'immigrant crime wave' is a campaign ad, not a statistic.

title: Karl Data Narrative: U.S. murders fell sharply in 2023 and 2024, among the larges
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: U.S. murders fell sharply in 2023 and 2024, among the largest drops on record]
[Source: FBI Uniform Crime Reporting data]

Crime fell. Fast. You'd never know from the news. Fear sells better than facts, and fear funds police budgets.

title: Karl Data Narrative: U.S. drug overdose deaths peaked above 100,000 a year before
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: U.S. drug overdose deaths peaked above 100,000 a year before declining in 2024]
[Source: CDC National Center for Health Statistics]

Fifty years of drug war, and overdoses hit record highs anyway. What finally helped was treatment, naloxone and harm reduction. Not more cages.

title: Karl Data Narrative: Prime-age employment reached its highest level in over two d
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: Prime-age employment reached its highest level in over two decades in 2023–2024]
[Source: Bureau of Labor Statistics]

'Nobody wants to work anymore' was never true. People are working. They just want to be paid enough to live.

title: Karl Data Narrative: The top 10% of households own about 90% of U.S. stock market
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: The top 10% of households own about 90% of U.S. stock market wealth]
[Source: Federal Reserve, Distributional Financial Accounts]

When the market hits a record, it's not your record. Most families' wealth is their home and whatever's left in checking.

title: Karl Data Narrative: Louisiana's voucher program led to significant declines in p
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: Louisiana's voucher program led to significant declines in participating students' math scores]
[Source: Abdulkadiroglu, Pathak & Walters, AEJ: Applied Economics (2018)]

School vouchers were sold as a ticket out. In Louisiana, kids who used them fell behind. Public money should stay in public schools.

title: Karl Data Narrative: Mondragon, a federation of worker cooperatives in Spain, emp
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: Mondragon, a federation of worker cooperatives in Spain, employs tens of thousands of worker-members]
[Source: Mondragon Corporation]

Workers owning their workplace isn't a fantasy. It's a multi-billion-euro operation that's survived for decades. Democracy works at work, too.

title: Karl Data Narrative: The Civil Liberties Act of 1988 paid $20,000 in reparations
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: The Civil Liberties Act of 1988 paid $20,000 in reparations to each surviving Japanese American incarcerated during WWII]
[Source: U.S. Congress, Civil Liberties Act of 1988]

The U.S. has paid reparations before. It apologized and wrote checks. Saying it's 'impossible' for slavery and Jim Crow is a choice, not a fact.

title: Karl Data Narrative: The federal government spends far more subsidizing homeowner
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: The federal government spends far more subsidizing homeowners through the tax code than on rental assistance for low-income families]
[Source: Center on Budget and Policy Priorities / Joint Committee on Taxation]

The biggest housing welfare program in America goes mostly to people who already own homes. The poor get waitlists. The comfortable get deductions.

title: Karl Data Narrative: Uber, Lyft, DoorDash and others spent about $200 million on
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: Uber, Lyft, DoorDash and others spent about $200 million on California's Prop 22 campaign in 2020]
[Source: California Secretary of State filings]

The most expensive ballot measure in state history was paid for by gig companies to make sure their drivers weren't employees. That's how much your rights were worth to them.

title: Karl Data Narrative: Americans hold an estimated $1 trillion-plus in credit card
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: Americans hold an estimated $1 trillion-plus in credit card debt]
[Source: Federal Reserve Bank of New York, Household Debt and Credit Report]

People aren't swiping for luxuries. They're swiping for groceries and car repairs. Credit cards became the safety net we never built.

title: Karl Data Narrative: Maternity care deserts cover about a third of U.S. counties
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: Maternity care deserts cover about a third of U.S. counties]
[Source: March of Dimes, Nowhere to Go (2024)]

In a third of counties, there's no hospital or birth center offering obstetric care and no obstetric providers. Rural mothers drive an hour in labor. Some don't make it.

title: Karl Data Narrative: A Lancet study estimated single-payer healthcare would save
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: A Lancet study estimated single-payer healthcare would save about 68,000 lives a year]
[Source: Galvani et al., The Lancet (2020, estimate)]

Universal healthcare isn't just a budget question. It's a body count question. Every year we wait, people die who didn't have to.

title: Karl Data Narrative: Gallup found about 70% of Americans approved of labor unions
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: Gallup found about 70% of Americans approved of labor unions in 2024]
[Source: Gallup (2024)]

Unions are more popular than either political party. The public's already on our side. Now we organize the workplace to match.

title: Karl Data Narrative: The Amazon Labor Union won the first successful union electi
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: The Amazon Labor Union won the first successful union election at a U.S. Amazon warehouse in 2022]
[Source: National Labor Relations Board, JFK8 election]

A group of warehouse workers with no national union backing beat one of the richest companies on Earth. Don't tell me it can't be done.

title: Karl Data Narrative: Hospitals and insurers spend a large share of U.S. health do
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: Hospitals and insurers spend a large share of U.S. health dollars on administration; one study put it at about a third]
[Source: Himmelstein et al., Annals of Internal Medicine (2020)]

We pay armies of people to bill, deny and fight over claims. Other countries spend that money on doctors.

title: Karl Data Narrative: Shell and BP scaled back climate targets in 2023–2024 as oil
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: Shell and BP scaled back climate targets in 2023–2024 as oil profits soared]
[Source: Company announcements, 2023–2024]

When it came down to the planet or the payout, they picked the payout. Never let a fossil fuel company grade its own homework.

title: Karl Data Narrative: Pre-pandemic, most workers who would benefit from a $15 fede
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: Pre-pandemic, most workers who would benefit from a $15 federal minimum wage were adults age 20 or older]
[Source: Economic Policy Institute (2021)]

The minimum wage isn't for teenagers' pocket money. It's for adults raising kids, paying rent and holding this economy together.

title: Karl Data Narrative: Very few estates pay the federal estate tax; the Tax Policy
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: Very few estates pay the federal estate tax; the Tax Policy Center estimated only around 80 small business and farm estates owed it in 2017]
[Source: Tax Policy Center (2017 estimate)]

The 'death tax kills family farms' story is a myth to protect dynastic fortunes. Billionaires hide behind farmers they've never met.

title: Karl Data Narrative: The 2017 tax law cut the corporate tax rate from 35% to 21%
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: The 2017 tax law cut the corporate tax rate from 35% to 21%]
[Source: Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017]

The richest corporations got a permanent cut. Most workers got a small, temporary one. Then the buybacks broke records.

title: Karl Data Narrative: About 3.7 million people are on probation or parole
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: About 3.7 million people are on probation or parole]
[Source: Bureau of Justice Statistics / Prison Policy Initiative (approximate)]

Millions live one technical violation away from a cell. Miss a meeting, lose a job, go back. Supervision has become a revolving door.

title: Karl Data Narrative: Fewer than half of private-sector workers in the lowest wage
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: Fewer than half of private-sector workers in the lowest wage group have access to paid sick leave]
[Source: Bureau of Labor Statistics, National Compensation Survey (approximate)]

The workers handling your food are the ones who can't afford to stay home sick. That's a public health problem, not just a labor one.

title: Karl Data Narrative: About 37% of U.S. adults couldn't cover a $400 emergency exp
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: About 37% of U.S. adults couldn't cover a $400 emergency expense with cash or its equivalent in 2023]
[Source: Federal Reserve, Economic Well-Being of U.S. Households (approximate)]

One flat tire from crisis. That's the reality for tens of millions of people in the richest country in history.

title: Karl Data Narrative: In only a small fraction of U.S. counties can a full-time wo
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: In only a small fraction of U.S. counties can a full-time worker earning the prevailing minimum wage afford a one-bedroom at fair market rent]
[Source: National Low Income Housing Coalition, Out of Reach (approximate)]

Even a one-bedroom is out of reach on the minimum wage almost everywhere. Work full time, still can't afford a door that locks.

title: Karl Data Narrative: The U.S. has the highest per capita cumulative carbon emissi
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: The U.S. has the highest per capita cumulative carbon emissions of any major country]
[Source: Carbon Brief analysis (2021) / Global Carbon Project]

'China emits more now' is a dodge. America has put more carbon in the sky over time than any nation. We owe the most, and we can lead.

title: Karl Data Narrative: 146 garment workers died in the Triangle Shirtwaist Factory
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: 146 garment workers died in the Triangle Shirtwaist Factory fire in 1911, many behind locked doors]
[Source: Cornell University ILR, Triangle Fire archive]

The bosses locked the exits to stop unauthorized breaks. Women jumped from the ninth floor. Every fire code you walk past was written in their blood.

title: Karl Data Narrative: The Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 created the first feder
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: The Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 created the first federal minimum wage, 25 cents an hour, and the 40-hour workweek]
[Source: U.S. Department of Labor]

The weekend wasn't a gift from the market. Workers fought, struck and died for it. Then they made it law.

title: Karl Data Narrative: The federal minimum wage hit its peak buying power in 1968,
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: The federal minimum wage hit its peak buying power in 1968, worth roughly $14 an hour in today's dollars]
[Source: Economic Policy Institute / Department of Labor (approximate)]

A minimum wage worker in 1968 could buy more than one today. We didn't get richer at the bottom. We went backwards.

title: Karl Data Narrative: The top federal income tax rate was 91% in the 1950s
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: The top federal income tax rate was 91% in the 1950s]
[Source: IRS / Tax Policy Center historical rates]

The decade conservatives call America's golden age taxed the richest at 91%. The middle class boomed. Funny how that works.

title: Karl Data Narrative: Corporate income taxes made up about a third of federal reve
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: Corporate income taxes made up about a third of federal revenue in the early 1950s and about a tenth in recent years]
[Source: Office of Management and Budget historical tables (approximate)]

Corporations used to pay their share. Now you pick up the slack through your paycheck. The burden didn't vanish. It moved onto you.

title: Karl Data Narrative: President Reagan fired about 11,000 striking air traffic con
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: President Reagan fired about 11,000 striking air traffic controllers in 1981]
[Source: PATCO strike, U.S. Department of Transportation records]

One firing told every boss in America that busting unions was open season. Wages have been stuck ever since. That's not an accident. It's a turning point.

title: Karl Data Narrative: The 1968 Memphis sanitation strike began after two workers w
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: The 1968 Memphis sanitation strike began after two workers were crushed to death in a garbage truck]
[Source: Martin Luther King Jr. Research and Education Institute, Stanford]

'I AM A MAN.' Black sanitation workers demanded dignity. Dr. King was killed standing with them. Labor rights and civil rights were always the same fight.

title: Karl Data Narrative: The 1914 Ludlow Massacre killed about 20 people, including w
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: The 1914 Ludlow Massacre killed about 20 people, including women and children, in a striking miners' tent colony]
[Source: Colorado Encyclopedia / historical records]

Company-backed guards set fire to the tents of striking families. That's how far bosses will go. Remember it when they call unions 'divisive.'

title: Karl Data Narrative: The Battle of Blair Mountain in 1921 was the largest armed l
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: The Battle of Blair Mountain in 1921 was the largest armed labor uprising in U.S. history, with around 10,000 coal miners]
[Source: West Virginia Encyclopedia]

Miners in red bandanas marched for the right to organize. The word 'redneck' was a badge of solidarity before it was an insult.

title: Karl Data Narrative: The Delano grape strike and boycott lasted from 1965 to 1970
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: The Delano grape strike and boycott lasted from 1965 to 1970 and won the first major farmworker union contracts]
[Source: United Farm Workers history]

Five years. Millions of shoppers refused grapes. Filipino and Mexican farmworkers stood together and won. A boycott is solidarity you can do at the grocery store.

title: Karl Data Narrative: The Montgomery bus boycott lasted 381 days
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: The Montgomery bus boycott lasted 381 days]
[Source: National Park Service / Montgomery Improvement Association history]

Black workers walked to their jobs for over a year rather than give in. The bus company bled money. Collective refusal breaks systems.

title: Karl Data Narrative: The Tulsa Race Massacre of 1921 destroyed about 35 blocks of
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: The Tulsa Race Massacre of 1921 destroyed about 35 blocks of the Greenwood district]
[Source: Oklahoma Historical Society / 2001 Tulsa Race Riot Commission]

A thriving Black business district was burned by a white mob. Insurance claims were denied. That's how wealth gaps are built: by force, then by paperwork.

title: Karl Data Narrative: Racially restrictive covenants were ruled unenforceable by t
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: Racially restrictive covenants were ruled unenforceable by the Supreme Court in 1948]
[Source: Shelley v. Kraemer, U.S. Supreme Court]

For decades, deeds literally banned Black families from buying homes. That's not ancient history. Your neighborhood map was drawn that way.

title: Karl Data Narrative: The Federal Housing Administration's underwriting manual in
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: The Federal Housing Administration's underwriting manual in the 1930s and 40s recommended against lending in Black and mixed neighborhoods]
[Source: FHA Underwriting Manual; Rothstein, The Color of Law]

The government didn't just allow segregation. It wrote it into mortgage rules. Then it called the results 'the market.'

title: Karl Data Narrative: Section 504 disability rights protesters occupied a San Fran
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: Section 504 disability rights protesters occupied a San Francisco federal building for about 26 days in 1977]
[Source: Disability Rights Education & Defense Fund]

Disabled activists slept on the floor, sustained by the Black Panthers and unions bringing food. They won. Solidarity across movements wins.

title: Karl Data Narrative: The Black Panther Party's Free Breakfast for Children Progra
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: The Black Panther Party's Free Breakfast for Children Program fed thousands of kids daily by 1969]
[Source: National Museum of African American History and Culture]

The Panthers fed kids before school while the government didn't. The federal School Breakfast Program became permanent a few years later. Mutual aid shames power into action.

title: Karl Data Narrative: The Americans with Disabilities Act passed in 1990 after act
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: The Americans with Disabilities Act passed in 1990 after activists crawled up the U.S. Capitol steps]
[Source: ADA history, National Archives]

Disabled protesters left their wheelchairs and dragged themselves up the steps. Rights aren't given. They're climbed for.

title: Karl Data Narrative: The Stonewall uprising in 1969 began as resistance to a poli
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: The Stonewall uprising in 1969 began as resistance to a police raid]
[Source: National Park Service, Stonewall National Monument]

Queer and trans people, many working class and people of color, fought back. Pride started as a riot against police harassment, not a corporate float.

title: Karl Data Narrative: The Cuyahoga River in Ohio caught fire in 1969, helping spur
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: The Cuyahoga River in Ohio caught fire in 1969, helping spur the creation of the EPA and the Clean Water Act]
[Source: Ohio History Connection / EPA]

A river was so polluted it burned. People got angry, and Washington moved. Every environmental law exists because ordinary people forced it.

title: Karl Data Narrative: The Deepwater Horizon explosion in 2010 killed 11 workers an
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: The Deepwater Horizon explosion in 2010 killed 11 workers and spilled roughly 134 million gallons of oil into the Gulf]
[Source: NOAA / U.S. Coast Guard]

Eleven workers died and the Gulf drowned in oil because BP cut corners. Louisiana fishermen are still paying for it.

title: Karl Data Narrative: Hurricane Katrina killed more than 1,800 people in 2005
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: Hurricane Katrina killed more than 1,800 people in 2005]
[Source: National Hurricane Center (approximate)]

The storm was natural. The levee failures, the abandoned poor, and the slow response were not. Disaster hits hardest where investment never came.

title: Karl Data Narrative: Louisiana expanded Medicaid in 2016, extending coverage to h
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: Louisiana expanded Medicaid in 2016, extending coverage to hundreds of thousands of working adults]
[Source: Louisiana Department of Health]

In a red state, expansion gave hundreds of thousands of people healthcare. Cooks, cashiers, offshore workers. It works when politicians let it.

title: Karl Data Narrative: Louisiana has one of the highest poverty rates in the countr
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: Louisiana has one of the highest poverty rates in the country, around 1 in 5 residents]
[Source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey (approximate)]

One of the richest oil and gas regions on Earth, and one in five people live in poverty. The wealth flows out. The pollution stays.

title: Karl Data Narrative: Farmers receive roughly 15 cents of every dollar Americans s
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: Farmers receive roughly 15 cents of every dollar Americans spend on food]
[Source: USDA Economic Research Service, Food Dollar Series (approximate)]

Farmers grow it. Workers process it. Middlemen and monopolies take the rest. Follow the dollar and you'll find who's squeezing whom.

title: Karl Data Narrative: Four companies control roughly 85% of U.S. beef packing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: Four companies control roughly 85% of U.S. beef packing]
[Source: USDA / Department of Justice reports (approximate)]

Ranchers get paid less. You pay more at the store. Four giants sit in the middle and pocket the difference. That's not a free market. It's a cartel.

title: Karl Data Narrative: More than 100 rural hospitals have closed or stopped inpatie
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: More than 100 rural hospitals have closed or stopped inpatient care since 2010]
[Source: UNC Sheps Center for Health Services Research (approximate)]

Rural America is losing its hospitals. When the ER is an hour away, heart attacks become death sentences.

title: Karl Data Narrative: The EU's Working Time Directive guarantees at least four wee
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: The EU's Working Time Directive guarantees at least four weeks of paid annual leave; the U.S. guarantees none by law]
[Source: European Commission / U.S. Department of Labor]

Europeans get a month off by law. Americans get whatever the boss allows, which is often nothing. Rest is a right, not a perk.

title: Karl Data Narrative: There is no federal law requiring paid sick leave for privat
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: There is no federal law requiring paid sick leave for private-sector workers in the U.S.]
[Source: U.S. Department of Labor]

Go to work sick or lose the shift. That's the choice millions face. A pandemic proved how dangerous that is for everyone.

title: Karl Data Narrative: Germany's codetermination law gives workers up to half the s
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: Germany's codetermination law gives workers up to half the seats on supervisory boards of large companies]
[Source: German Codetermination Act of 1976]

In Germany, workers sit on the board. Their economy didn't collapse. It builds cars and machines the world buys. Democracy at work works.

title: Karl Data Narrative: Union density in Denmark is roughly two-thirds of workers
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: Union density in Denmark is roughly two-thirds of workers]
[Source: OECD / ICTWSS database (approximate)]

No national minimum wage, because unions win better than one. That's what labor power looks like when most workers are organized.

title: Karl Data Narrative: Norway's sovereign wealth fund holds well over $1 trillion f
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: Norway's sovereign wealth fund holds well over $1 trillion from oil revenue]
[Source: Norges Bank Investment Management (approximate)]

Norway treated its oil as public wealth. Louisiana let companies take it. Same resource, very different results for working people.

title: Karl Data Narrative: The 1986 Anti-Drug Abuse Act punished crack cocaine 100 time
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: The 1986 Anti-Drug Abuse Act punished crack cocaine 100 times more harshly than powder cocaine]
[Source: U.S. Sentencing Commission]

Same drug, different form, different neighborhoods. The 100-to-1 rule filled prisons with Black men for decades. Congress cut it to 18-to-1 in 2010. It's still not one.

title: Karl Data Narrative: Roughly two-thirds of people held in local jails have not be
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: Roughly two-thirds of people held in local jails have not been convicted of a crime]
[Source: Prison Policy Initiative (approximate)]

Most people in jail are legally innocent. They're there because they can't afford bail. Freedom shouldn't have a price tag.

title: Karl Data Narrative: The U.S. is the only country known to sentence people to lif
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: The U.S. is the only country known to sentence people to life without parole for crimes committed as children]
[Source: Human Rights Watch / Campaign for the Fair Sentencing of Youth]

Kids. Life in prison. No chance of release. Every other nation decided that was wrong.

title: Karl Data Narrative: The UN's Mandela Rules define solitary confinement beyond 15
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: The UN's Mandela Rules define solitary confinement beyond 15 consecutive days as prolonged and prohibit it]
[Source: United Nations Standard Minimum Rules for the Treatment of Prisoners]

U.S. prisons have held people in solitary for years, even decades. The UN calls that cruel. We call it Tuesday.

title: Karl Data Narrative: In Rucho v. Common Cause (2019), the Supreme Court ruled fed
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: In Rucho v. Common Cause (2019), the Supreme Court ruled federal courts can't hear partisan gerrymandering claims]
[Source: U.S. Supreme Court]

Politicians pick their voters, and the Court said that's not its problem. Map-drawing is power. Draw them fairly or the people lose.

title: Karl Data Narrative: Wyoming and California each get two U.S. senators, though Ca
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: Wyoming and California each get two U.S. senators, though California has about 67 times more people]
[Source: U.S. Census Bureau]

A vote in Wyoming counts many times more than a vote in California in the Senate. That's not democracy. That's math rigged in 1787.

title: Karl Data Narrative: Washington, D.C. has about 700,000 residents and no voting m
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: Washington, D.C. has about 700,000 residents and no voting member of Congress]
[Source: U.S. Census Bureau]

More people than Wyoming, paying federal taxes, with no vote in Congress. Taxation without representation is printed on their license plates.

title: Karl Data Narrative: Janus v. AFSCME (2018) ended mandatory fair-share fees for p
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Statistic: Janus v. AFSCME (2018) ended mandatory fair-share fees for public sector unions nationwide]
[Source: U.S. Supreme Court]

Billionaire-funded groups spent years bringing this case. The goal was always to drain unions. Teachers, nurses and firefighters kept organizing anyway.
